Project Summary — NEXUS × BIOSKIN

NEXUS × BIOSKIN is an integrated astronaut health-monitoring system developed by Team Sağlık Olsun! to support health management during long-duration space missions.

Our project combines BIOSKIN, a functional ESP32-based hardware prototype, with NEXUS, an interactive health-monitoring dashboard. BIOSKIN uses DHT11 and MAX30100 sensors to collect temperature, humidity, heart rate, and blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂) data, transmitting measurements to NEXUS through a local Wi-Fi network.

Beyond physical measurements, NEXUS incorporates experimental facial fatigue indicators using MediaPipe, voice analysis through the Web Audio API, and NASA research-based bone density loss simulations. The platform brings these indicators together to provide understandable alerts, recommendations, and decision-support information.

Our solution addresses the challenge by transforming separate health measurements into a unified monitoring experience that may help astronauts recognize potential health changes during extended missions.

Unlike a purely conceptual proposal, we developed and tested a working hardware-software prototype.

Our long-term vision is to improve sensor accuracy, offline functionality, and portability, with potential applications in remote healthcare on Earth.

NEXUS × BIOSKIN aims to transform health data into meaningful insights—both in space and on Earth.

details:
NEXUS × BIOSKIN — Project Details

Project Overview

NEXUS × BIOSKIN is an integrated astronaut health-monitoring system developed by Team Sağlık Olsun! for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our project addresses the challenges of monitoring astronaut health during long-duration space missions by combining real-time sensor measurements, experimental behavioral analysis, NASA-based research scenarios, and decision-support features into a single platform.

How Does It Work?

Our system consists of two interconnected components:

1. BIOSKIN — Physical Health-Monitoring Prototype

BIOSKIN is an ESP32-based hardware prototype developed and assembled by our team. It integrates:

  • DHT11: Measures environmental temperature and humidity.
  • MAX30100: Provides heart rate and blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂) readings.
  • ESP32: Processes sensor readings and transmits them to NEXUS through a local Wi-Fi network.
  • You can access our ESP32 BIOSKIN device which has DHT11, O2 sensor, MAX30100, cardiac sensor and etc. from our PowerPoint presentation in Google Drive. Thanks for your interest.

2. NEXUS — Integrated Monitoring Dashboard

NEXUS is a web-based software platform that brings multiple monitoring features together:

  • Real-Time Monitoring: Displays BIOSKIN sensor measurements and their changes over time.
  • Facial Analysis: Uses Google's MediaPipe technology to monitor eye closure and mouth-opening patterns as experimental indicators of possible fatigue.
  • Voice Analysis: Uses the Web Audio API to compare successive voice recordings against a personal reference, examining changes in acoustic characteristics.
  • Bone Health Simulation: Uses published NASA research on spaceflight-related bone loss to visualize hypothetical changes over mission duration. Exercise, sleep, and nutrition inputs support exploratory scenario comparisons rather than validated individual predictions.
  • Alerts and Recommendations: Organizes available measurements and experimental indicators into understandable status messages and suggested next steps.
  • Scientific References: Provides an integrated question-and-answer section supported by NASA publications and other technical sources.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The primary goal of NEXUS × BIOSKIN is to make complex health information more accessible and understandable during extended space missions.

Rather than presenting isolated measurements, our system brings different indicators together to support health awareness and informed decision-making.

In future applications, the same approach could support remote health monitoring on Earth, particularly in rural areas or environments with limited access to healthcare services.

Technologies and Tools Used

Hardware: ESP32 development board, DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor, MAX30100 pulse oximetry sensor, electronic components, and custom wiring.

Programming and Software: C++ with Arduino IDE for the ESP32 firmware; HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the web-based NEXUS dashboard; MediaPipe for facial landmark analysis; and Web Audio API for voice processing.

Communication: Local Wi-Fi networking and HTTP-based sensor data exchange.

Scientific Foundation: NASA Human Research Program publications, NASA Technical Reports Server, NASA-STD-3001, and supporting technical documentation.

Creativity and Innovation

Our project's originality lies in integrating physical sensor hardware, behavioral indicators, scientific simulations, and user-oriented guidance within one coherent system.

Instead of developing a conventional dashboard that only displays sensor readings, we designed NEXUS × BIOSKIN to connect multiple sources of information and present them in a more meaningful context.

We developed and tested a functional hardware-software prototype during the hackathon, demonstrating that our concept extends beyond a theoretical design.

Design Considerations and Future Development

Throughout development, our team considered technical feasibility, accessible hardware, scientific transparency, connectivity limitations, usability, and the importance of distinguishing measured data from experimental interpretations.

NEXUS × BIOSKIN is currently a research prototype, not a clinically validated medical device. Its facial and voice indicators are exploratory, and the bone-health module does not directly measure bone density.

Our next steps include validating sensors against reference devices, improving data security and offline capabilities, making BIOSKIN more portable, and conducting further testing.

Our vision is to transform health data into meaningful insights that can support human well-being, both in space and on Earth.
